Pargalı Ibrahim Pasha: Grand Vizier of the Ottoman Empire from 1523 to 1536. Pargalı Ibrahim Pasha (c. 1495 – 15 March 1536), was the first grand vizier of the Ottoman Empire appointed by Sultan Suleiman the Magnificent.

Governing France during the childhood of Louis XV, whom he was related to as both great-nephew and first cousin twice removed, this early 18th-century regent married a daughter of Louis XIV — who is he?
Philippe II, Duke of Orléans: Regent of France from 1715 to 1723.
What single word names the practice of banning by law the making, selling, and drinking of alcoholic beverages?

Rooted in a Greek word meaning 'to snatch away' from First Thessalonians, this end-times evangelical belief holds that living and dead Christians alike will rise to meet Christ in the clouds — what is it called?
This three-time Conservative prime minister, who doubled as Foreign Secretary for most of his tenure, championed a foreign policy he called 'splendid isolation' — who was he?
Robert Cecil, Viscount Cecil of Chelwood
Robert Gascoyne-Cecil, 3rd Marquess of Salisbury: British prime minister (1885-86; 1886-92; 1895-1902)
This Emir led Kuwait from 2006 until his death in 2020, having been the fourth son of a previous ruling sheikh — who was he?
Sabah Al-Ahmad Al-Jaber Al-Sabah: Emir of Kuwait from 2006 to 2020.
Anointed by the prophet Samuel as the first king of a newly unified Israelite kingdom, he died falling on his own sword after defeat by the Philistines at Mount Gilboa — who was he?
Saul: Biblical figure and Israelite monarch.
Known by the kunya Abu Idris, this Chechen guerrilla commander helped recapture Grozny in 1996 and later masterminded some of Russia's worst hostage-taking attacks — who is he?

After revealing Zeus's abduction of a nymph to a river god and later cheating death itself, this mythical king of Corinth was condemned to forever push a boulder up a hill, only to watch it roll back down — who is he?
Sisyphus: King of Ephyra in Greek mythology.
This Indonesian general became his country's second president in 1967, two years after his troops put down an attempted coup — who is he?
Suharto: President of Indonesia from 1967 to 1998.
Named to the Time 100 "Heroes" list, this ethologist transformed humane livestock handling and was among the first autistic people to publish insights from her own experience — who is she?
Temple Grandin: American academic and autism activist (born 1947)
This retired Royal Navy vice admiral served as an equerry to Queen Elizabeth II before marrying her only daughter in 1992 — who is he?
Timothy Laurence: Retired Royal Navy officer (born 1955)

This liberal religious tradition has no single creed, instead uniting congregations through shared covenants centered on love and pluralistic worship, drawing on everything from Christianity to Buddhism — which faith tradition?
Unitarian Universalism: Non-creedal liberal religious movement.
The youngest presidential candidate in the 2024 Republican primaries, this Harvard and MIT graduate founded a biotech company and is now seeking the Ohio governorship. Who is he?
Vivek Ramaswamy: American entrepreneur and politician (born 1985)

Controlling most of Eastern Galicia from late 1918 to mid-1919, this short-lived state also claimed parts of northern Bukovina and Carpathian Ruthenia, with power held by a nationalist democratic party — what was it called?
West Ukrainian People's Republic: 1918–1919 state in Central Europe.
This man is the younger brother of China's current top leader, and serves as president of an international energy conservation and environmental protection association — who is he?
Xi Yuanping: Son of Xi Zhongxun, brother of Xi Jinping.
China's premier through the 1980s, he was the architect of political reform — until his support for the 1989 Tiananmen Square protests cost him all his power. Who is this fallen reformer?
Who among these was born first?
Stephen Hales (born 1677) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four was born earliest?
John Ray (born 1627) is the earliest of the four. John Ray (29 November 1627 – 17 January 1705) was an English Christian naturalist and one of the earliest English parson-naturalists.
Which of these four dates back furthest?
MUMPS (founded 1966) is the earliest of the four.
Which one below was established earliest?

Fortran (founded 1957) is the earliest of the four. Fortran (formerly FORTRAN) is a third-generation, compiled, imperative programming language designed for numeric computation and scientific computing.
Who among these is an astronomer?
John Flamsteed is an astronomer. John Flamsteed (19 August 1646 – 31 December 1719) was an English astronomer and the first Astronomer Royal.
Which of these is a mathematician?
Grigori Perelman is a mathematician. The full details of Perelman's work were filled in and explained by various authors over the following several years.
What is the atomic number of Radon?
Radon is a chemical element; it has symbol Rn and atomic number 86.
What is the atomic number of Gallium?
Gallium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ga and atomic number 31.
In what year was Edward Witten born?
Edward Witten: Witten is a researcher in string theory, quantum gravity, supersymmetric quantum field theories, and other areas of mathematical physics.
In what year was Milton Friedman born?
Milton Friedman: Friedman's challenges to what he called "naive Keynesian theory" began with his interpretation of consumption, which tracks how consumers spend.
In what year was Karl Marx born?
Karl Marx: Born in Trier in the Kingdom of Prussia, Marx earned a doctoral degree in philosophy from the University of Jena in 1841.
In what year did Alexander Graham Bell die?
Alexander Graham Bell: Bell considered his invention an intrusion on his real work as a scientist and refused to have a telephone in his study.
In what year did Max Planck die?
Max Planck: Max Karl Ernst Ludwig Planck (German: [ˈmaks ˈplaŋk]; 23 April 1858 – 4 October 1947) was a German theoretical physicist.
In what year was Boron discovered?
Boron is a chemical element; it has symbol B and atomic number 5.
Dopamine: Pfizer. Dopamine (DA, a contraction of 3,4-dihydroxyphenethylamine) is a neuromodulatory molecule that plays several important roles in cells.
In which country is TAI TF Kaan?
TAI TF Kaan: Turkey. Designed to replace the Turkish Air Force’s fleet of F-16 Fighting Falcons, the Kaan is also intended for export to international markets.
Who is credited with discovering Leo Minor?
Leo Minor: Johannes Hevelius. Leo Minor is a small and faint constellation in the northern celestial hemisphere.
Who is credited with discovering Graph theory?
Graph theory: Leonhard Euler. In mathematics and computer science, graph theory is the study of graphs, which are mathematical structures used to model pairwise relations between objects.
Who is credited with discovering Budesonide?
Budesonide: Ralph Brattsand. Budesonide, sold under the brand name Pulmicort, among others, is a steroid medication.
Who is credited with discovering Platinum?
Platinum: Julius Caesar Scaliger. Platinum is a chemical element; it has symbol Pt and atomic number 78.
These large seabirds of the tubenose order range widely across the Southern Ocean and North Pacific, but are notably absent from the North Atlantic today. What birds are they?
Albatross are large seabirds related to the procellariids, storm petrels, and diving petrels in the order Procellariiformes (the tubenoses).
This English number theorist became a mathematical legend by proving Fermat's Last Theorem, earning the 2016 Abel Prize and a knighthood. Who is he?
Andrew Wiles (born 11 April 1953) is an English mathematician and a Royal Society Research Professor at the University of Oxford, specialising in number theory.
Which noble gas, symbol Ar and atomic number 18, is the third most abundant gas in Earth's atmosphere — more plentiful there than carbon dioxide or neon?
Argon is a chemical element; it has symbol Ar and atomic number 18.
Created in 1989 by Brian Fox for the GNU Project as a free replacement for the Bourne shell, this command-line interpreter became the default login shell on countless Linux systems — which shell?
Bash (Unix shell) (short for "Bourne Again SHell") is an interactive command interpreter and command language developed for Unix-like operating systems.
A flowering vine native to South Asia, this plant's small dried red drupes become the world's most traded spice, its final coloring depending on how ripe the fruit was when harvested — which spice?
Black pepper (Piper nigrum) is a flowering vine in the family Piperaceae, cultivated for its fruit (the peppercorn), which is usually dried and used as a spice and seasoning.
Also known as undulant fever and Malta fever, this zoonotic illness spreads mainly through drinking unpasteurized milk and is caused by tiny coccobacilli — what is it?
Brucellosis is a zoonosis (zoonotic disease) spread primarily via ingestion of unpasteurized milk from infected animals.

Once thought to not really exist as a stable molecule, this compound was confirmed since around 1990 to have a real, if fleeting, existence — lasting only about 20 milliseconds at body temperature — what compound is it?
Carbonic acid is a chemical compound with the chemical formula H2CO3.

This perennial flowering herb is the only species of its onion-relative genus native to both the New World and Old World, prized for its edible leaves and flowers and also used to repel insects. What herb is this?
Chives is a species of flowering plant in the family Amaryllidaceae.
Part of the same species as cabbage and broccoli, this loose-leafed member of the 'kale group' has been grown for its big, dark-green leaves since classical antiquity — what is it?
Collard (plant) is a group of loose-leafed cultivars of Brassica oleracea (the same species as many common vegetables, including cabbage and broccoli).
Together with birds, this order of predatory reptiles is one of only two survivors of the ancient Archosauria — and it lumps together alligators, caimans, and gharials. What is it?
Crocodilia is an order of semiaquatic, predatory reptiles that are known as crocodilians.

Named from the Latin word for 'finger' because of its tubular, spike-borne flowers, this genus of about 20 European and West Asian species was reclassified into a new plant family in 2001 — what is it commonly called?
Digitalis (or) is a genus of about 20 species of herbaceous perennial plants, shrubs, and biennials, commonly called foxgloves.
This American physicist was the first to make a transuranium element, neptunium, sharing the 1951 Nobel Prize in Chemistry with Glenn Seaborg. Who was he?
Edwin McMillan (September 18, 1907 - September 7, 1991) was an American physicist credited with being the first to produce a transuranium element, neptunium.
Co-founder of MIT's J-PAL poverty lab, she shared a 2019 Nobel with her husband and Michael Kremer for using randomized trials against global poverty — who is it?

Esther Duflo (born 25 October 1972) is a French-American economist currently serving as the Abdul Latif Jameel Professor of Poverty Alleviation and Development Economics at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT).

With over 2,400 described species, these soft-bodied beetles produce light mainly at twilight, an ability that likely began as a larval warning signal before evolving into an adult mating display. Name this insect family?
Firefly are a family of elateroid beetles with more than 2,400 described species, many of which are light-emitting.
First studied scientifically by an Augustinian friar experimenting with pea plants in 19th-century Brno, this branch of biology examines heredity and trait inheritance — which field?
Genetics is the study of genes, genetic variation, and heredity in organisms.
Designed in the late 1950s as a replacement for the piston-engined E-1 Tracer, this twin-turboprop U.S. Navy aircraft provides carrier-based early warning radar coverage. Name the aircraft?
Grumman E-2 Hawkeye is an American all-weather, carrier-capable, tactical airborne early warning (AEW) aircraft.
Named after the physicist who first proved the existence of electromagnetic waves, this SI unit measures one cycle per second. What unit is it?
Hertz (symbol: Hz) is the unit of frequency in the International System of Units (SI), often described as being equivalent to one event (or cycle) per second.
Triggered by causes like vomiting, diarrhea, or the diuretic furosemide, this condition denotes a blood potassium level under 3.5 mmol/L — what is it?
Hypokalemia is a low level of potassium (K+) in the blood serum.
Known for the mantra 'Dying is not a crime,' this euthanasia advocate served eight years in prison after his fourth trial ended in a murder conviction — who is he?
Jack Kevorkian (May 26, 1928 - June 3, 2011), also known by the nickname "Dr.
While tinkering with electromagnets, which American physicist discovered self-inductance and later became the very first secretary of the Smithsonian Institution?
Joseph Henry (December 17, 1797- May 13, 1878) was an American physicist and inventor who served as the first secretary of the Smithsonian Institution.
Home to aromatic herbs like mint, oregano, and lavender as well as the seed crop chia, this family of mostly herbaceous flowering plants is commonly known as the mints or deadnettles — which family?

Lamiaceae is a family of flowering plants commonly known as mints, deadnettles, or sages. The mint family as a whole has a cosmopolitan distribution comprising about 236 genera and around 6,900 to 7,200 species.
This ACE inhibitor can take up to four weeks for full effect and is also used to prevent kidney problems in people with diabetes — which medication?
Lisinopril is a medication belonging to the drug class of angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors and is used to treat hypertension (high blood pressure), heart failure, and heart attacks.
Recognizable by the male's iridescent green head, this widespread dabbling duck species has been introduced to countries from New Zealand to South Africa far beyond its native range — what is it?
Mallard (Anas platyrhynchos) is a dabbling duck that breeds throughout the temperate and subtropical Americas, Eurasia, and North Africa.
Crushed leaves of this mint-family herb smell like spearmint, yet it has caused deaths when used as a traditional abortifacient — which species, also known as pennyroyal?

Mentha pulegium (European) pennyroyal, or pennyrile, also called mosquito plant and pudding grass, is a species of flowering plant in the mint family, Lamiaceae, native to Europe, North Africa, and the Middle East.
A small terrestrial carnivore of the family Herpestidae that feasts mainly on insects, reptiles, and birds — and turns up as an introduced pest in Hawaii — what creature is it?
Mongoose is a small terrestrial carnivorous mammal belonging to the family Herpestidae.
A naval aviator who flew the F9F Panther in Korea before commanding Apollo 11, this Ohio-born engineer earned a place in history in 1969 — who is he?
Neil Armstrong (August 5, 1930 - August 25, 2012) was an American astronaut and aeronautical engineer who, as the commander of the 1969 Apollo 11 mission, became the first person to walk on the Moon.
Named after a German physicist, this SI unit of electrical resistance is represented by the uppercase Greek letter omega — name the unit?
Ohm (symbol:, the uppercase Greek letter omega) is the unit of electrical resistance in the International System of Units (SI).
Found in organs such as the brain and lungs, inside flatworms, and within leaf cross-sections, this word names an organism's bulk functional tissue — what is it?
Parenchyma is the bulk of functional substance in an animal organ such as the brain or lungs, or a structure such as a tumour.
Written by the Hong sisters, this South Korean series about young mages dealing with heaven and earth aired on tvN in two parts during 2022 and 2023. What show is it?
Pharynx (pl.: pharynges) is the part of the throat behind the mouth and nasal cavity, and above the esophagus and trachea (the tubes going down to the stomach and the lungs respectively).
Cough, chest pain, fever, and trouble breathing point to this infection of the lungs' alveoli, often classified by where it was caught — community or hospital — what is it?
Pneumonia is an inflammatory condition of the lung primarily affecting the small air sacs known as alveoli.
This rose-family genus of roughly 340 species includes almonds, apricots, and cherries, whose pit encloses a kernel that's edible in some species and poisonous in others — which genus?

Prunus is a genus of flowering trees and shrubs from the family Rosaceae, with about 340 accepted species (as of March 2024) that include peaches and nectarines, apricots, plums, cherries and almonds.
Belonging to the genus Ribes and native to western Europe, which berry carries the scientific name Ribes rubrum and has spread into the wild in many regions?
Redcurrant (Ribes rubrum) is a member of the genus Ribes in the family Grossulariaceae.
Mostly used in wear-resistant electrical contacts and thick-film resistors, which rare, chemically unreactive platinum-group metal has atomic number 44?
Ruthenium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ru and atomic number 44.

This potentially life-threatening condition occurs when the body's dysregulated response to infection damages its own tissues and organs, often causing fever, rapid heartbeat, and confusion — what is it called?
Sepsis is a potentially life-threatening condition that arises when the body's dysregulated response to infection causes injury to its own tissues and organs.
Found throughout the nightshade family — including in potato leaves, fruit, and tubers — this saponin-family toxin doubles as the plant's own natural pesticide. What compound is it?
Solanine is a glycoalkaloid poison found in species of the nightshade family within the genus Solanum, such as the potato (Solanum tuberosum).
A Jamaican-British Marxist sociologist who co-founded New Left Review, this thinker became a founding figure of the Birmingham School of Cultural Studies — who was he?
Stuart Hall (cultural theorist) (3 February 1932 - 10 February 2014) was a Jamaican-British Marxist sociologist, cultural theorist, and political activist.
This American actress won an Oscar, three BAFTAs, two Tonys, and two Emmys, one of only 24 performers ever to complete acting's Triple Crown. Who is she?
Terry Gou (pinyin: Gu Timng; Peh-e-j: Koeh Ti-bng; born 18 October 1950) is a Taiwanese billionaire businessman and politician.
Caused by superantigens from staph or strep bacteria, this condition brings fever, a sunburn-like rash, and peeling skin, and has been tied to absorbent tampon use — which condition?
Toxic shock syndrome (TSS) is a condition caused by bacterial toxins.
This member of the herpesvirus family causes chickenpox in children and, upon reactivation later in life, shingles in adults — what is it called?
Varicella zoster virus (VZV), also known as human herpesvirus 3 (HHV-3, HHV3), is one of nine known herpes viruses that can infect humans.
Short-legged, muscular, and stubby-tailed, this Australian marsupial can reach about a metre long and tip the scales between 20 and 35 kilograms — what is it?
Wombat are short-legged, muscular quadrupedal marsupials of the family Vombatidae that are native to Australia.
Accidentally discovered in 1967 by German chemist Karl Clauss at Hoechst AG, which calorie-free artificial sweetener is sold under the brand names Sunett and Sweet One?

Designed to replace the Lockheed C-130 Hercules and sized between it and the Boeing C-17, this four-engine European turboprop military transporter first flew from Seville in December 2009 despite nearly being cancelled over cost overruns. What's the aircraft?
Airbus A400M Atlas: Multi-national four-engine turboprop military transport aircraft.
This mushroom genus contains the notorious 'death cap,' responsible for roughly 90% of all fatal mushroom poisonings worldwide — which genus?
Amanita: Genus of mushrooms. The genus is responsible for 95% of fatalities resulting from mushroom poisoning, with the death cap accounting for 90% of fatalities every year.

This psychological term describes reduced motivation or ability to experience pleasure, recognized in the DSM-5 as a component of depressive, substance-related, psychotic, and personality disorders. What is it called?
Nicknamed the 'Primeval Bird' in German, this magpie-sized, feathered dinosaur from 150-million-year-old Jurassic Germany was long hailed as the earliest known bird — what is it?
Archaeopteryx: Extinct genus of bird-like dinosaurs.
Sold under the brand name Strattera, this selective norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor treats ADHD and is only recommended for patients age six and up — what is this medication?
Atomoxetine: Medication used to treat ADHD.
Second only to the capybara among living rodents and able to top 50 kg, this animal sports chisel-like incisors, webbed back feet, and a flat, scaly tail — what is it?
This portmanteau of 'binary digit' is the most basic unit of information in computing, representing one of two possible states like 0 or 1 — eight of them make up a byte. What is it?
Bit: Unit of information. The bit represents a logical state with one of two possible values.

Unlike most elements, this one is forged entirely by cosmic-ray spallation and supernovae rather than stellar fusion, and is mined from evaporite minerals like borax, mostly in Turkey — which element?
Boron: Chemical element with atomic number 5 (B)
Encompassing reporting, dashboards, data mining, and analytics, this set of strategies and technologies helps companies turn raw data into strategic decisions — what's it called?
Business intelligence: Strategies for analysis and use of data.
Domesticated in Mexico roughly 6,000 years ago, this nightshade produces berries used in cooking, medicine, and even self-defense sprays — which plant species is it?
Capsicum annuum: Species of flowering plant in the nightshade family.
Originally called 'centigrade' from Latin words for a hundred and steps, this SI temperature scale was renamed in 1948 to honor the Swedish astronomer who proposed it in 1742 — which scale?
Celsius: Unit of measurement for temperature.
Once common as the refrigerant "Freon," these carbon-chlorine-fluorine compounds were phased out under the Montreal Protocol for chewing through the ozone layer — what are they?
Home to jellyfish, corals, and sea anemones, this phylum of aquatic invertebrates is defined by specialized stinging cells used to capture prey — what is it?
Cnidaria: Aquatic animal phylum having cnidocytes.

This physician was convicted of involuntary manslaughter in 2011 after inadvertently overdosing his famous patient with the anesthetic propofol, which he had been improperly using as a sleep aid — who is he?
Conrad Murray: American physician and convicted felon (born 1953)
Encompassing roadrunners, koels, and anis among its roughly 150 species, this widespread bird family favors trees but includes some ground-dwellers — what is it?
Cuckoo: Family of birds. The cuckoo family includes the common or European cuckoo, roadrunners, koels, malkohas, couas, coucals, and anis.
This biological process, powered by rhythmic muscle waves called peristalsis, expels solid waste from the digestive tract through the anus or cloaca — what is it?
Defecation: Expulsion of feces from the digestive tract.
A dentist and gambler who fought alongside lawman Wyatt Earp at the O.K. Corral, his reputation claimed dozens of killings though researchers count just one to three — who was this gunfighter?
Doc Holliday: Gambler, gunfighter, and dentist in the American West (1851–1887)
Now the wealthiest Brazilian and the richest person in Singapore, this Facebook co-founder later started the venture firm B Capital — who is he?
Coiled to just 6 to 7 centimetres but stretching nearly 20 feet if unraveled, this tube connects each testicle to the vas deferens and stores maturing sperm — what is it?

Epididymis: Tube that connects a testicle to a vas deferens. The epididymis serves as an interconnection between the multiple efferent ducts at the rear of a testicle (proximally), and the vas deferens (distally).
The most widely distributed member of its subfamily, this semiaquatic, fish-eating mustelid ranges across Europe, much of Asia, and North Africa's Maghreb — which animal?
Discovered in the fallout debris of the first hydrogen bomb test in 1952 and named for a pioneer of nuclear physics, this element 100 is the heaviest you can make by neutron bombardment. What is it?
Fermium: Chemical element with atomic number 100 (Fm)
This American physician-scientist led the Human Genome Project before directing the NIH for over a decade under three presidents — who guided the mapping of our DNA?
Once Mexico's top law-enforcement official as secretary of public security, this man was convicted in a Brooklyn courtroom in 2023 for taking millions in bribes from the Sinaloa Cartel — who is he?
Genaro García Luna: Mexican politician and convicted felon (born 1968)
One of the very first animals domesticated — in Iran some 10,000 years ago — this Bovidae cousin of the sheep now numbers over 1.1 billion worldwide, 150 million of them in India; what is it?

This French civil engineer made his name building railway bridges like the Garabit Viaduct and later helped erect the Statue of Liberty, before retiring to study meteorology and aerodynamics — who was he?

Spun into usable fiber some 50,000 years ago and, alongside bamboo, among the fastest-growing plants on Earth, which Cannabis sativa crop is grown for rope, paper, textiles and biofuel rather than for getting high?
These giant wasps of the genus Vespa build communal nests from chewed wood pulp, with one Asian species growing past two inches long — what are they called?

When the thyroid produces too little hormone, the body slows down — cold intolerance, fatigue, constipation, weight gain — and worldwide too little dietary iodine is the leading cause. What's the condition?
Hypothyroidism: Insufficient production of thyroid hormones.
Known naturally as the mineral hematite, this reddish compound with formula Fe2O3 is the main source for the steel industry and gets reduced by aluminum in the fiery thermite reaction — what is it?
Iron(III) oxide: Chemical compound. It occurs in nature as the mineral hematite, which serves as the primary source of iron for the steel industry.
This businessman and chemist owned the Lakers through their 1980s 'Showtime' era, winning 10 NBA titles before a Hall of Fame induction as a contributor — who was he?
Jerry Buss: American businessman and investor (1933–2013)
The first woman of Indian origin to fly to space, she served as a mission specialist on two Space Shuttle Columbia flights, the second ending in the 2003 disaster that killed her — who was she?
Born of Peranakan Chinese cuisine, this spicy Southeast Asian noodle dish is often served in a rich coconut-curry soup soured with tamarind — what is it?
Laksa: Spicy noodle dish from Southeast Asia.
This fibrous connective tissue links bone to bone in every one of the 30,000 known amniote species, and in birds it even anchors flight feathers to bone — what is it?

This Canadian physicist worked on the Manhattan Project determining critical mass values for uranium and plutonium, and in 1946 was fatally exposed to radiation in a lab accident at Los Alamos — who is he?
Louis Slotin: Canadian physicist and chemist (1910–1946)
Nicknamed sea cows, these slow-moving herbivorous mammals graze on more than 60 kinds of aquatic plants in the Caribbean, the Amazon basin, and West Africa — what are they?
Manatee: Genus of mammals. The main causes of death for manatees are human-related issues, such as habitat destruction and human objects.
Diagnosis, prognosis, prevention, treatment and palliation of injury and disease — drawing on biomedical science, genetics and technology — define this science and practice. What is it?

Medicine: Diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of illness. Medicine encompasses a variety of health care practices which evolved to maintain and restore health through the prevention and treatment of illness and infection.
Son of a U.S. vice president, this young art collector vanished in 1961 during an expedition into New Guinea's Asmat region, with some accounts claiming he was killed by local tribesmen — who was he?
Michael Rockefeller: American anthropologist and art collector (1938–1961)
Originally a dry-season staple for ǃKung hunter-gatherers, this tropical vine in the Cucurbitaceae family produces an intensely bitter edible fruit widely used across Asian cuisine — what is it?
Momordica charantia: Species of plant in the gourd family.
Most often triggered by a viral infection and capable of progressing to heart failure or cardiac arrest, which condition involves inflammation of the heart muscle itself?

Myocarditis: Inflammation of the heart muscle. Myocarditis can progress to inflammatory cardiomyopathy when there is associated ventricular remodeling and cardiac dysfunction due to chronic inflammation.
This Danish physicist won the 1922 Nobel Prize for a model of the atom in which electrons leap between discrete, stable orbits around the nucleus — who is he?

Symbolized by the Greek letter omega, this SI unit of electrical resistance was named after a 19th-century German physicist and, since 2019, is defined as an exact value based on fundamental constants — what unit is it?
Ohm: SI derived unit of electrical resistance. The ohm (symbol: Ω, the uppercase Greek letter omega) is the unit of electrical resistance in the International System of Units (SI).
Making up most of Earth's crust, this class of chemical compound pairs oxygen with another element — the same chemistry behind the thin protective layer on aluminium foil — what is it called?
Oxide: Compounds containing an oxygen atom.
Born in the Soviet Union, this entrepreneur co-founded a social network in 2006 before developing a messaging app now headquartered in Dubai — who is he?

Approved for medical use in the US back in 1959 and sold under the brand name Adipex-P, this appetite-suppressing stimulant is a substituted amphetamine used alongside diet and exercise to treat obesity — what is it?
Its name comes from the Spanish for 'little silver,' yet this dense, stubbornly unreactive metal — element 78 — is so scarce only a few hundred tonnes are mined a year. Which one?
Platinum: Chemical element with atomic number 78 (Pt)

Arising over 60 million years ago from small tree-dwellers, this order favored big brains, binocular color vision and opposable thumbs to grasp among the branches — and it includes lemurs and apes — what is it?
Primate: Order of mammals. New primate species continue to be discovered: over 25 species were described in the 2000s, 36 in the 2010s, and six in the 2020s.

Known in France as the Patou and in the US by another name, this French livestock guardian breed hails from a range straddling France and Spain, protecting flocks from wolves and bears. What breed is it?
Pyrenean Mountain Dog: French breed of dog. The Pyrenean Mountain Dog (Chien de Montagne des Pyrénées) is a French breed of livestock guardian dog.
From a startled jump to a cat automatically reorienting itself mid-fall, this involuntary, split-second reaction runs through the nervous system without needing conscious thought — what's it called?
Reflex: Automatic, involuntary response to a stimulus.
Usually hidden underground, this plant organ anchors it in place while drawing in water and nutrients — what is it?
Root: Basal organ of a vascular plant.

With ears set low to detect prey moving underground and furry paw soles that insulate against scorching ground, this small desert feline was first described in the Algerian Sahara in 1858 — which animal?
Sand cat: Small wild cat species (Felis margarita)

Nicknamed the 'last Soviet citizen' for being aboard Mir when the USSR dissolved, this cosmonaut flew six missions and helped connect the first Russian and American modules of a space station — who is he?
Sergei Krikalev: Soviet and Russian cosmonaut (born 1958)

Thanks to extra joints in its skull, this legless, scale-covered reptile can swallow prey far bigger than its own head — and its paired organs sit one behind the other to fit a narrow body. What creature is it?
Working largely in isolation, this early-20th-century Indian mathematician solved problems thought unsolvable, though leading professionals first dismissed his work as too novel — who was he?

A retired US Navy captain, this NASA astronaut became the first woman to fly on an orbital spacecraft's test flight in 2024 and had her ISS stay extended by more than nine months due to technical issues — who is she?
Sunita Williams: U.S. Navy officer and NASA astronaut (born 1965)
A math prodigy who abandoned academia in 1969 for a reclusive cabin life, the 'Unabomber' mailed bombs for 17 years and published a 35,000-word anti-technology manifesto — who was he?
Native to the Mediterranean and containing roughly 350 aromatic species, this herb genus lends its name to a common seasoning found in kitchens worldwide — which genus?
About 70% of people infected with this parasite-caused sexually transmitted infection show no symptoms at all, though it can raise the risk of contracting HIV — what condition is it?
Trichomoniasis: Medical condition. Trichomoniasis (trich) is an infectious disease caused by the parasite Trichomonas vaginalis.
